title: Why the Worst GTA Game Is One Rockstar Could Never Make Today
description: Polygon reflects on GTA Advance, exploring how one of the worst games in the series served as an essential stepping stone for modern GTA greatness ahead of GTA6.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Looking Back at a Forgotten Chapter

In the expansive and legendary history of the *Grand Theft Auto* franchise, not every title achieved the monumental, generation-defining success of entries like *GTA V*. Recently, gaming media outlet Polygon published a retrospective on one of the series' more polarizing entries: *GTA Advance*. While it is widely regarded by many as one of the worst games in the franchise, it remains an essential stepping stone for what makes GTA great today.

As anticipation continues to build for *GTA6*, looking back at how Rockstar Games evolved through its experimentation provides fascinating context. Early spin-offs and constrained hardware projects forced developers to test boundaries, figure out core mechanics, and understand what players truly loved about the open-world formula.

## A Stepping Stone for Modern Design

Today, the industry standards for open-world games are unimaginably high, with massive budgets, hyper-realistic graphics, and complex systems. Because of how the gaming landscape has shifted, Polygon notes that a project like *GTA Advance* is essentially something Rockstar could never make today. The sheer scale and expectations surrounding modern titles mean small-scale, experimental handheld spin-offs belong firmly to a different era.

However, the lessons learned from these early hurdles contributed directly to the DNA of the franchise. It is reasonable to suggest that the foundational design philosophies forged during those challenging years helped pave the way for the incredible depth and scale we anticipate in upcoming milestones like *GTA6*.

## Editor's Take

Polygon's look back at *GTA Advance* serves as a great reminder that great franchises aren't built overnight. Acknowledging the missteps and rough experiments of the past highlights just how far the genre has come, making the wait for *GTA6* all the more interesting for longtime fans.
